key_insight: The Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark links image appearance, camera motion and surface mechanics to evaluate deformable 3D reconstruction with persistent material correspondence.
engineering_relevance: It supports controlled testing of reconstruction and displacement-estimation methods under camera motion, surface deformation and mechanical-prior mismatch.
method: Generate and annotate tubular scenes with the open-source LumenMorph toolkit.
Cross three surface-motion conditions with moving and stationary cameras across six baseline scene families.
Track material points using persistent triangle identities and weights, with separate geometric and mechanical consistency checks.
evidence_signal: The release contains 5,580 RGB images and includes structure-from-motion, optical-flow and supplied-geometry displacement-interpolation studies that distinguish registration coverage from geometric accuracy.
watch_item: The benchmark is synthetic and does not claim anatomical or clinical realism; matched appearance variants cover only moving-camera finite-element actions in four families.
paper_title: Synthetic Deformable Tubular Benchmark: A mechanically annotated dataset for evaluating deformable 3D reconstruction
